newsitem.title: CHINA: First Shanghai-HK rail link to be completed by Jly.
newsitem.headline: First Shanghai-HK rail link to be completed by Jly.

text.p: The first rail link between Shanghai and Hong Kong will be completed before the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, a spokesman for the Shanghai Railway Bureau said on Wednesday.
"We need final approval from the Ministry of Railways on when we can make the link through to Hong Kong," the spokesman told Reuters.
"Anyway, the line will reach Hong Kong before July 1," he said, declining to give further details.
The first train will make its inaugural journey form Shanghai on April 1, the Shanghai-based Business News said.
But the train will not travel the more than 1,000 km (620 miles) to Hong Kong. It will instead stop in the city of Guangzhou, 124 km (77 miles) inside the Chinese border.
The newspaper said that once the line was operational, one train a day would leave Shanghai for Kowloon, in Hong Kong.
The newspaper did not detail how much the Shanghai Bureau of Railways had invested in the rail link, apart from saying it was a huge amount.
